stem: Why is neuroimaging, specifically an MRI, recommended when cerebral palsy is suspected?

options.text: Because MRI results are abnormal in approximately $89\%$ of CP cases
To determine if the child has Down Syndrome
Because it is the only way to diagnose spasticity
To check for spinal muscular atrophy

explanation: Since CP involves disruptions to motor tracts, imaging usually reveals these structural abnormalities in the vast majority of cases.
rationale: Think about the high likelihood of visualizing damage to the motor pathways in the brain.

optionExplanations.A: Since CP involves disruptions to motor tracts, imaging usually reveals these structural abnormalities in the vast majority of cases.
optionExplanations.B: Down Syndrome is a genetic diagnosis typically identified through clinical features and genetic testing, not primarily by brain MRI.
optionExplanations.C: Spasticity is a clinical finding determined through physical examination of muscle tone and reflexes.
optionExplanations.D: Spinal muscular atrophy is a neuromuscular disorder usually diagnosed through genetic testing or EMG, not brain MRI.

source.hint: Think about the high likelihood of visualizing damage to the motor pathways in the brain.
